questions.q: Why does this lesson deliberately stay at a conceptual level instead of teaching Bicep syntax in depth?
options: Because Terraform & Bicep for Data Engineers already has dedicated lessons for hands-on Bicep authoring, and repeating that would be a worse copy of a course that already does it properly
Because Bicep cannot be used to deploy Azure SQL resources
Because DP-300 does not cover infrastructure as code at all
Because ARM templates have been fully retired by Microsoft
questions.explain: This course avoids duplicating a course that already covers Bicep authoring in depth, and points there instead.

questions.q: Exactly which course and lesson does this lesson point to for hands-on Bicep authoring and a real deployment walkthrough?
options: Terraform & Bicep for Data Engineers, Lesson 15, "Deploying Azure SQL With Bicep"
T-SQL Development, Lesson 15
Git/GitHub & CI/CD for Data, Lesson 20
This same course's Lesson 15
questions.explain: Lesson 15 of Terraform & Bicep for Data Engineers is the verified, hands-on Bicep deployment lesson, including a real Azure Portal deployment-history screenshot.

questions.q: What is the relationship between ARM templates and Bicep, per this lesson?
options: Bicep is a cleaner syntax that compiles down to the same underlying ARM templates
They are two completely unrelated Azure services with no connection
ARM templates are written in Bicep syntax natively
Bicep replaced ARM's resource provider entirely, and ARM templates no longer function
questions.explain: ARM templates are the underlying JSON format; Bicep compiles to that same format in a much more concise syntax.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what three benefits does infrastructure as code give a DBA even if someone else writes it?
options: Repeatable deployments, reviewable changes via pull request, and an auditable git history of changes
Faster query execution, better indexing, and automatic statistics updates
Free compute, unlimited storage, and no need for backups
Elimination of all firewall and network configuration
questions.explain: These three — repeatable, reviewable, auditable — are the concrete reasons this lesson gives for a DBA to care about IaC.

questions.q: What Azure resource type does the lesson's minimal Bicep example declare?
options: Microsoft.Sql/servers/databases
Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines
Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts
Microsoft.Network/virtualNetworks
questions.explain: The example declares a database resource as a child of an existing SQL server, at the S3 service tier.
